'''Roderick Neil Brown''', [[Queen's Counsel|Q.C.]]<ref>
{{Cite web |url=http://www.albertahumanrights.ab.ca/20131028_1330_01_han.pdf 
|title=Province of Alberta -The 28th Legislature - First Session - Alberta Hansard
|issue=60 
|access-date=2016-10-26 
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140325210012/http://www.albertahumanrights.ab.ca/20131028_1330_01_han.pdf 
|archive-date=2014-03-25 |date=October 28, 2013 
|url-status=dead }}</ref> is a lawyer, biologist, [[Canadians|Canadian]] politician and former Member of the [[Legislative Assembly of Alberta]], representing the constituency of [[Calgary Nose Hill|Calgary-Nose Hill]] as a [[Progressive Conservative Association of Alberta|Progressive Conservative]].

==Early life==

Brown was born in [[Calgary]], and earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] in [[biology]] from the [[University of Calgary]] in 1971. He subsequently earned a [[Master of Science]] in [[zoology]] from the [[University of Alaska]] in 1974 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in biology from [[McGill University]] in 1977. He worked as an assistant professor of biology at [[Trent University]] before returning to the University of Calgary to earn his [[Bachelor of Laws]], which he received in 1982. He worked for McLaws and Company (now Parlee McLaws LLP) in civil litigation before opening his own practice in 1987.<ref name="leg bio">{{Cite web|url=https://www.assembly.ab.ca/home?p=mla_bio&rnumber=21|title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta|website=www.assembly.ab.ca}}</ref>

==Political career==

Brown first sought election in the [[2004 Alberta general election|2004 provincial election]], when he ran as the [[Progressive Conservative Association of Alberta|Progressive Conservative]] candidate in the newly formed [[Calgary-Nose Hill (provincial electoral district)|Calgary-Nose Hill]].  He defeated his closest challenger, [[Alberta Liberal Party|Liberal]] Len Borowski, by more than 1,500 votes.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://elections.ab.ca/Public_Website/files/Statements/21.pdf |title=2004 Alberta provincial election results, Calgary-Nose Hill |accessdate=2008-03-28}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref> During his first term, in addition to his responsibilities as an MLA, Brown served as chair of both the Private Bills Committee and the Conflicts of Interest Act Review Committee. He was also a member of the Cabinet Policy Committee on Resources and the Environment, the Standing Committee on Government Services, the MLA Committee on AISH Review, the MLA Committee on Métis Harvesting, the Agenda and Priorities Committee, the Public Accounts Committee, and the Legislative Review Committee. He also served as chair of the Alberta Forestry Research Institute.<ref name="leg bio"/>

Brown faced Borowski again in the [[2008 Alberta general election|2008 election]], and defeated him by a similar margin.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://results.elections.ab.ca/21.htm |title=Alberta 2008 provincial election results, Calgary-Nose Hill |accessdate=2008-04-07 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090301032216/http://results.elections.ab.ca/21.htm |archivedate=March 1, 2009 }}</ref>

Currently, in addition to his duties as MLA for Calgary-Nose Hill, Brown serves as chair of the Private Bills Committee and is a member of the Standing Committee on Public Safety and Services. He also holds the position of chair of the Cabinet Policy Committee on Public Safety and Services with Responsibilities to the departments of Executive Council, Treasury Board, Justice, Aboriginal Relations, Solicitor General and Public Security, and Service Alberta.<ref name="leg bio"/>

===Legislative initiatives===

Although he has never been a cabinet minister, Brown has sponsored a large number of government bills, all of which have passed through the legislature.<ref name="2005 bills">{{cite web |url=https://www.assembly.ab.ca/pro/bills/s-bill05.htm |title=Bill Status Report for the 26th Legislature - 1st Session (2005) |accessdate=2008-04-14 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20061005105724/http://www.assembly.ab.ca/pro/bills/s-bill05.htm |archivedate=2006-10-05 }}</ref><ref name="2006 bills">{{cite web |url=https://www.assembly.ab.ca/pro/bills/s-bill06.htm |title=Bill Status Report for the 26th Legislature - 2nd Session (2006) |accessdate=2008-04-14 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604234239/http://www.assembly.ab.ca/pro/bills/s-bill06.htm |archivedate=2011-06-04 }}</ref><ref name="2007 bills">{{cite web|url=https://www.assembly.ab.ca/pro/bills/s-bill07.htm |title=Bill Status Report for the 26th Legislature - 4th Session (2007) |accessdate=2008-04-14 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604234245/http://www.assembly.ab.ca/pro/bills/s-bill07.htm |archivedate=2011-06-04 }}</ref>  The ''Business Corporations Amendment Act'' was a 2005 bill that made a variety of changes to the management of [[corporations]] domiciled in Alberta, including prohibiting accountants who owned shares in a corporation from acting as its auditor.<ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_1%5C20050323_1330_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=March 23, 2005}}</ref>  [[Alberta Liberal Party|Liberals]] [[Mo Elsalhy]], [[Harry B. Chase]], and [[Dan Backs]] spoke in support of the bill, although [[Alberta New Democratic Party|New Democrat]] [[Raj Pannu]] expressed concern that a provision that created [[unlimited liability]] corporations would flood Alberta with ''de facto'' American corporations that were registered in Alberta but did their business elsewhere.<ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_1%5C20050411_2000_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=April 11, 2005}}</ref><ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_1%5C20050502_2000_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=May 2, 2005}}</ref>  This bill was followed by the ''Business Corporations Amendment Act (No. 2)'', which provided protection for minority shareholders in the event that a corporation was converted to unlimited liability over opposition, and which clarified the period during which former shareholders in unlimited liability corporations remained liable.<ref name="November 28">{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_1%5C20051128_2000_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=November 28, 2005}}</ref>  It passed with Liberal support, although Pannu expressed concern that the new protections were not sufficient.<ref name="November 28"/><ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_1%5C20051130_1330_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=November 30, 2005}}</ref>  Also in 2005, Brown sponsored the ''Employment Pension Plans Amendment Act'', which implemented uncontroversial changes to the regulation of private pensions and which received support from all parties.<ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_1%5C20050517_1330_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=May 17, 2005}}</ref>

Brown sponsored two government bills in 2006.<ref name="2006 bills"/>  The ''Persons with Developmental Disabilities Community Governance Amendment Act'' dissolved the Persons with Developmental Disabilities Provincial Board and transferred its authority to the Minister of Seniors and Community Supports, while expanding the authority of the six regional boards.<ref name="April 24">{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_2%5C20060424_2000_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=April 24, 2006}}</ref>  MLAs from all parties, including Liberals [[Bharat Agnihotri]], [[Hugh MacDonald (Canadian politician)|Hugh MacDonald]], and [[Bridget Pastoor]], [[Alberta Alliance]] leader [[Paul Hinman]], and New Democrats [[Ray Martin (politician)|Ray Martin]], [[Brian Mason]], and [[Raj Pannu]], supported the bill.<ref name="April 24"/><ref>{{cite hansard | url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_2%5C20060511_1330_01_han.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061208000300/http://www.assembly.ab.ca/ISYS/LADDAR_files/docs/hansards/han/legislature_26/session_2/20060511_1330_01_han.pdf|archive-date=8 Dec 2006|title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta |url-status=live | date=May 11, 2006}}</ref>  The ''Health Information Amendment Act'' made a number of changes to the conditions under which health information would be disclosed, including preventing the automatic reporting of private information to [[United States of America|American]] authorities under the [[PATRIOT Act]].<ref name="April 25">{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_2%5C20060425_2000_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=April 25, 2006}}</ref>  New Democrats Pannu and [[David Eggen]] and Liberals Elsalhy, Pastoor, and [[Bruce Miller (politician)|Bruce Miller]] spoke in favour of the bill, although Liberal [[Laurie Blakeman]] expressed reservations that the content of the bill didn't reflect the recommendations of the legislature's special committee whose work led to the bill.<ref name="April 25"/><ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_2%5C20060503_2000_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=May 3, 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_2%5C20060516_2000_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=May 16, 2006}}</ref>

In 2007, Brown sponsored one of the new [[Ed Stelmach]] government's flagship pieces of legislation, the ''Conflicts of Interest Amendment Act'', which lengthened the cooling off period during which cabinet ministers and other high-ranking members of government to engage in certain activities after leaving the government's employment.<ref>{{cite news |first=Chloé |last=Fedio |publisher=Vue Weekly |title=It's bills, bills, bills (oh, and royalties, of course) as Legislature gets set to resume |date=October 31, 2007 |url=http://www.vueweekly.com/article.php?id=7235 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130205201823/http://www.vueweekly.com/article.php?id=7235 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=February 5, 2013 |accessdate=2008-04-14 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/alberta-to-tighten-conflict-of-interest-rules-for-top-bureaucrats-legislators-1.693317 |title=Alberta to tighten conflict-of-interest rules for top bureaucrats, legislators |date=April 19, 2007 |accessdate=2015-05-23}}</ref>  It also placed a requirement on MLAs that they report any personal litigation in which they were engaged, and was supported by all parties.<ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_3%5C20070502_1300_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=May 2, 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_3%5C20070509_2000_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=May 9, 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_3%5C20071204_2000_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=December 4, 2007}}</ref>  The same year he sponsored the ''Limitation Statutes Amendment Act'', which was also supported by the opposition and which amended Alberta's [[statute of limitations]] for some civil matters.<ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_3%5C20070411_1300_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=April 11, 2007}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_3%5C20070614_1300_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=June 14, 2007}}</ref>  Finally, Brown sponsored the ''Appeal Procedures Statutes Amendment Act''.  This bill made some amendments to the procedures of the [[Alberta Court of Appeal]].<ref name="April 17">{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_3%5C20070417_1300_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=April 17, 2007}}</ref>  It was supported by Liberals Elsalhy and [[Maurice Tougas]], but Pannu expressed some concern with a provision that would have made the keeping of transcripts of procedures discretionary.<ref name="April 17"/><ref>{{cite hansard |title=Legislative Assembly of Alberta| url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files%5Cdocs%5Chansards%5Chan%5Clegislature_26%5Csession_3%5C20070418_1300_01_han.pdf | house=Legislative Assembly of Alberta | date=April 18, 2007}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Brown has made a number of notable contributions to the public sector; he served on the Board of Governors and Senate of The University of Calgary, was Past-president of the Alumni Association of The University of Calgary, and was member of Student Legal Aid at The University of Calgary.  He also held the titles of Vice-president and chair of his Community Association, Associate (voting) member of the Royal Canadian Legion for over 25 years, Director of the Midnapore Church of England Society (historic site), and Lecturer at the Historic Calgary Week of Chinook Country Historical Society.  Brown also volunteered with the Booster Club of Thorncliffe-Greenview Community Association and canvassed for the Canadian Cancer Society, the Kidney Foundation, the Heart and Stroke Foundation, and the Alberta Lung Association.<ref name="leg bio"/>

In recognition of his commendable work, he has received a number of prestigious awards and honours including: National Research Council of Canada Scholar, National Sciences and Engineering Research Council grant, Chief Justice McGillivray Shield (University of Calgary, Faculty of Law), President's Citation (University of Calgary Students’ Union), Award of Merit Honoree (Alumni Association of the University of Calgary), Canada 125 Medal for Service to Community and Canada, and the Alberta Centennial medal for outstanding service to Alberta.<ref name="leg bio"/>

Brown enjoys various activities such as curling, canoeing, hunting, and fishing, in addition to creative writing, reading, and traveling.<ref name="leg bio"/> He identifies [[John A. Macdonald]] and [[Winston Churchill]] as his political heroes.<ref name="Calgary Sun">{{cite news|url=http://www.calgarysun.com/election/candidates.html |title=Calgary candidate profiles, Alberta election 2008 |publisher=[[Calgary Sun]] |accessdate=2008-04-16 |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20080304160950/http://www.calgarysun.com/election/candidates.html |archivedate=2008-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
